grammar.title: Subject pronouns with 'ser' (to be)
grammar.explanation: Spanish often drops the subject pronoun because the verb ending already shows who is speaking: (yo) soy, (tú) eres, (él/ella) es. Use 'soy' for permanent identity — 'Soy Ana' (I am Ana) — not 'estoy', which is for temporary states.

examples.translation: Hi, my name is Sofía. And you?
Nice to meet you, Sofía. I'm Diego.

content.tip: Practice greetings out loud at the actual time of day they're used — 'buenos días' in the morning, 'buenas tardes' after noon — so the timing becomes automatic.

grammar.title: Numbers agreeing with gender
grammar.explanation: 'Uno' becomes 'un' before a masculine noun (un café) and 'una' before a feminine one (una manzana). Numbers 200-900 also change: doscientos libros, doscientas manzanas.

content.tip: Count everyday objects around you in Spanish — stairs, plates, chairs — for thirty seconds a day.

grammar.title: 'Quisiera' for polite requests
grammar.explanation: 'Quisiera' (a softened past-subjunctive form of querer) is the standard polite way to order, gentler than 'quiero'. Follow it directly with the noun: 'Quisiera la sopa.'

examples.text: Quisiera una mesa para dos, por favor.
examples.translation: I would like a table for two, please.
What do you recommend for dessert?

content.tip: Rehearse ordering your actual favorite meal in Spanish before you next visit a Spanish or Latin restaurant.

grammar.title: Regular preterite endings (-ar verbs)
grammar.explanation: For a completed action in the past, drop -ar and add: -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron. 'Visitar' → 'visité' (I visited), 'visitó' (he/she visited). -er/-ir verbs use -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron instead.

examples.text: Ayer visité el museo con mi hermana.
examples.translation: Yesterday I visited the museum with my sister.

examples.text: Comimos en un restaurante muy bueno.
examples.translation: We ate at a very good restaurant.

content.tip: Tell one short story about yesterday out loud, using only past-tense verbs, before checking a dictionary.

grammar.title: 'Ir a' + infinitive for the near future
grammar.explanation: To talk about a plan already decided, use ir (voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van) + a + infinitive: 'Voy a estudiar esta noche' (I'm going to study tonight).

examples.text: ¿Estás libre el sábado? Voy a ver una película.
examples.translation: Are you free Saturday? I'm going to watch a movie.
Maybe, I'll let you know tomorrow.

content.tip: Add a specific day and time to every plan you practice — vague plans are harder to remember.
